summary:
The DaVinci International Film Festival (DIFF) is a Los Angeles festival celebrating independent filmmakers and screenwriters. Founded in 2017 by filmmaker Chadwick Pelletier, it is produced by the nonprofit DaVinci Film Society, a registered 501(c)(3).

DIFF presents films, screenplays, industry events, and awards, including its top Leo Awards. Its programs include the Storyline screenwriting competition, DaVinci Labs, ultra-short films, and documentaries. After moving online during the COVID-19 pandemic, the festival returned to in-person screenings at AMC Theatres at The Grove in Los Angeles.

The seventh edition, held in October 2025, launched FilmAfrica to promote African cinema. The initiative plans an independent awards platform in Nairobi in 2026, in partnership with the Swahili Village Group and Kenya Film Commission. DIFF also held its first DaVinci Masquerade in Cannes in May 2025 to support its international expansion.

The eighth edition took place in Los Angeles in September 2026, presenting a Visionary Award to writer-director Randall Wallace and introducing the RiseUP impact initiative.
